purpose: Fluconazole is used to treat fungal infections, including yeast infections of the vagina, mouth, throat, and other parts of the body. It can also treat fungal infections in the blood or internal organs. Doctors sometimes prescribe it to prevent fungal infections in people with weakened immune systems.
how_it_works: Fluconazole works by attacking the outer shell of the fungal cell, called the cell membrane. It blocks a substance the fungus needs to keep its cell wall intact, causing the fungal cell to break down and die. Your own body cells are not affected the same way, so it targets the fungus specifically.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, nausea, stomach upset, diarrhea, and dizziness. Some people may notice a mild skin rash. These side effects are usually not serious and often go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as fluconazole is processed through these organs. It can interact with many other medications, including blood thinners like warfarin, so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist. Rarely, it can cause serious liver problems or a severe allergic reaction — seek medical help immediately if you notice yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe rash, or difficulty breathing. Avoid this medication if you are pregnant unless your doctor specifically approves it.
typical_dosing: For a simple vaginal yeast infection, it is usually just one 150 mg tablet taken by mouth as a single dose. For other types of infections, dosing may be once daily for several days or weeks depending on the infection. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed, and finish the full course even if you feel better.
